condition: persistent adherent rough white patch on the left lateral tongue for 6 weeks in a 25-year daily cigarette smoker
level_rationale: A rough adherent white patch persisting for 6 weeks on the left lateral border of the tongue in an adult who smoked cigarettes daily for 25 years represents a high-risk potentially malignant oral mucosal lesion requiring dentist or oral-medicine evaluation and biopsy, whereas that same 6-week lateral tongue lesion actively gushing bright red blood indicates brisk lingual arterial hemorrhage with aspiration and airway risk requiring immediate emergency department care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing (quad_b, quad_c) + sourced accidental-biting causal belief clause (-att, Azhar 2018) + single-fact lingual hemorrhage escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive facts (25 years of daily cigarette smoking, 6-week adherent white patch on the left lateral tongue, and rough surface texture) avoiding 'does not rub off' stated negatives, with a 1-word span difference (26 vs 27 words), orthogonal 2x2 syntax-by-vocabulary crossing, and identical digit multisets across all 8 variants. Under reviewer_notes Rule A, replacing only f3 ('that feels rough') on the same 6-week tongue lesion with 'that is gushing bright red blood' escalates care cleanly inside the same oral case from dentist biopsy evaluation (level 3) to emergency department hemorrhage control (level 4).
